introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0580 Physics 1, June 2024, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Constants printed on the paper: acceleration due to gravity on the earth's surface $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; speed of light in a vacuum $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; charge on an electron $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section 1 (questions 1-42) has independent questions; Section 2 (questions 43-50) has two groups of questions about a practical situation (Questions 43-46 on Figure 5 and Questions 47-50 on Figure 6).

figures.legende: Four graphs of pressure P (vertical axis) against depth h (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A is a straight line rising from the origin, B is a straight line falling from a point on the P axis, C is a horizontal line, D is a curve that falls and flattens out (Question 12).

Four graphs of temperature theta (vertical axis) against time t (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A is a straight line rising from the origin, B is a straight line falling from a point on the theta axis, C is a curve rising more and more steeply from the origin, D is a horizontal line (Question 23).
Circuit with resistor R2 in series with a parallel pair formed by R1 (upper branch) and R3 (lower branch) (Question 28).

Four graphs of velocity v (vertical axis) against time t (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A is a straight line falling from a point on the v axis, B is a curve rising from the origin and levelling off, C is a curve rising from the origin with an increasing slope, D is a straight line rising from the origin (Question 35).

Sonometer: tuning fork at the left end of a vibrating string, paper rider on the string, a variable length marked between the fork end bridge and the movable bridge, a fixed bridge, and the string passing over a pulley to slotted masses (Questions 43-46).

Production unit transformer M (primary on an a.c. source, fewer turns than the secondary) joined by two transmission cables to the consumption unit transformer N, whose secondary feeds a diode P in series with the radio set R (Questions 47-50).

questions.enonce_markdown: A physical quantity is defined as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A physical quantity is a property of matter or of a phenomenon that can be measured and expressed as a number with a unit (mass, length, time, temperature...). An object (A, C) is not a quantity, and a measurement (D) is the act of finding the value of a quantity, not the quantity itself. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: any object that takes part only in physical activities
any measurement that is done in physics

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following pairs consists of one vector and one scalar quantity?
questions.corrige_markdown: A vector has magnitude and direction; a scalar has magnitude only. Moment (turning effect) and force are both vectors (A); energy and power are both scalars (B); velocity and momentum are both vectors (D). Force is a vector and distance is a scalar, so only option C pairs one of each. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following affects the force between two charged bodies?
questions.corrige_markdown: By Coulomb's law the force between two point charges is $F = \dfrac{k\,Q_1 Q_2}{d^2}$: it depends on the size of the charges and on the distance $d$ between them (it decreases as the distance increases). Mass, weight and speed do not appear in the law. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The change in momentum of a body is the same as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Impulse is defined as force $\times$ time, $Ft$, and by Newton's second law $Ft = mv - mu$, which is the change in momentum. The turning effect of a force is its moment; inertia depends on mass only, so it does not change with momentum. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A machine is a system that multiplies:
questions.corrige_markdown: A machine (lever, pulley, inclined plane...) lets a small effort overcome a larger load, so it multiplies the force applied; the mechanical advantage is $\dfrac{\text{load}}{\text{effort}}$. No machine can multiply energy (it would break the law of conservation of energy); the power is not multiplied either, because some energy is always wasted. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An object has weight of 100 N on the earth's surface. Its weight on a planet with acceleration due to gravity of $1.6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ is:
questions.corrige_markdown: With $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (value printed on the paper) the mass is $m = \dfrac{W}{g} = \dfrac{100}{10} = 10\ \mathrm{kg}$. Mass does not change from one planet to another, so on the planet $W = mg = 10 \times 1.6 = 16\ \mathrm{N}$. (Equivalently $W \propto g$: $100 \times \dfrac{1.6}{10} = 16\ \mathrm{N}$.) Option C comes from dividing by $1.6$ instead of multiplying. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A body travelling with a velocity of $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ accelerates at $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ to attain a velocity of $11\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The time taken for this change of velocity to take place is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $v = u + at$, so $t = \dfrac{v - u}{a} = \dfrac{11 - 5}{2} = 3\ \mathrm{s}$. Option A ($\frac{2}{6}$) inverts the ratio. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The density of iron decreases when it is heated because its:
questions.corrige_markdown: Density is $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$. Heating gives the iron more energy but it does not gain or lose matter, so its mass is constant. The solid expands, its volume increases and therefore its density decreases. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The law 'the extension of an elastic material is directly proportional to the applied force provided the elastic limit is not exceeded' is:
questions.corrige_markdown: This is the statement of Hooke's law, $F = ke$, valid up to the elastic limit. Ohm's law links voltage and current, Newton's first law concerns bodies at rest or in uniform motion, and Faraday's law concerns induced e.m.f. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The phenomenon where a body is made to vibrate at its natural frequency due to another body vibrating with that same frequency is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Resonance occurs when a system is driven at its natural frequency by another vibrating body, so that it vibrates with a large amplitude (a swing pushed at the right rhythm, a paper rider on a string and a tuning fork...). Interference, diffraction and refraction are wave behaviours that do not involve driving a body at its natural frequency. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The formation of a new atom after a radioactive decay process is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: When a nucleus emits an alpha or beta particle its proton number changes, so it becomes the nucleus of a different element: this change of one element into another is called transmutation. Ionization is the removal of electrons from an atom. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 1 shows how the pressure, $P$, of an object in a liquid changes with depth, $h$?

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In a liquid, $P = h\rho g$: the pressure is directly proportional to the depth, so the graph of $P$ against $h$ is a straight line through the origin with a positive gradient $\rho g$. This is graph A. Graph B would mean the pressure falls with depth, C that it is constant and D that it falls and levels off. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A fish at the bottom of a pond appears to be nearer to the surface because of the phenomenon of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Light rays from the fish bend away from the normal as they leave the water (a denser medium) for the air. The eye traces the rays back in a straight line and sees an image of the fish at a smaller depth: the real depth is greater than the apparent depth. This is refraction. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The tracks of alpha particles are thick and straight because:
questions.corrige_markdown: An alpha particle is heavy (4 atomic mass units), so it is hardly deflected by the air molecules it meets and travels in a straight line. It is also strongly ionizing: it knocks electrons off many molecules along its path, which makes a dense, thick track in a cloud chamber. Alpha particles are in fact the slowest of the three radiations (A is false); being positively charged or being helium nuclei describes what they are, not why the tracks look thick and straight. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the particles are massive and highly ionizing.

questions.enonce_markdown: The unit of power is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Power is the rate of doing work: $P = \dfrac{W}{t}$, so its unit is joule per second, $\mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$, called the watt. $\mathrm{N\,s}$ is the unit of impulse (change of momentum). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A block of mass 3 kg, lying on a platform has a potential energy of 240 J. What is the height of the platform?
questions.corrige_markdown: $E_p = mgh$, so $h = \dfrac{E_p}{mg} = \dfrac{240}{3 \times 10} = 8\ \mathrm{m}$ (with $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ given on the paper). Option D ($\frac{240}{3}$) forgets $g$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify who from the list below is doing work.
questions.corrige_markdown: Work is done when a force moves its point of application in the direction of the force: $W = F \times d$. The girl moves her own weight up the stairs, so she does work against gravity. The boy, the woman and the man exert forces (holding a bag or a child, or turning pages) without moving the load in the direction of the force, so no work is done in the physics sense. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: A boy standing in front of a class and carrying a bag of cement.
A girl playing and running up and down stair case.
A woman sitting on a chair and carrying a child.
A man sitting in his office and reading a book.

questions.enonce_markdown: Eggs float in salt water but sink in fresh water because:
questions.corrige_markdown: A body floats when its average density is less than the density of the liquid. The egg is denser than fresh water (it sinks) but less dense than salt water (it floats), so salt water is denser than fresh water. Dissolved salt adds mass without adding much volume. Option B is false (an iron nail sinks in salt water). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: salt water contains impurities, while fresh water does not.
all solids float in salt water
salt water is denser than fresh water.
fresh water is denser than salt water.

questions.enonce_markdown: Passengers getting out of a car that has been moving for a while sometimes get electric shocks because:
questions.corrige_markdown: As the car moves, friction between its body and the air molecules transfers charges to the car, which is insulated from the ground by its tyres. When a passenger touches the charged body and the ground, the charge flows through the passenger and gives a small shock. The battery does not charge the body (A), and the passengers do not charge by rubbing against each other (D). Option C describes charged air depositing charge, not the friction that produces the charge. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the car battery causes charges to build up on the surface of the car.
charges due to friction with air molecules are deposited on the surface of the car as it moves.
charged air molecules are deposited on the surface of the car as it moves.
the passengers in the car get charged as they rub against each other when the car is moving.

questions.enonce_markdown: A small electric oven with a power rating of 1000 W, 220 V would require a fuse of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The working current is $I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{1000}{220} \approx 4.5\ \mathrm{A}$. The fuse must be rated just above the normal current so that it does not blow in normal use but melts when the current becomes too large. 0.5 A and 1 A would blow at once; 7 A is well above the working current and would protect the wiring poorly. The suitable value is 5 A. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A virtual image is an image that:
questions.corrige_markdown: A virtual image is formed where rays only appear to come from (they do not actually meet), so it cannot be captured on a screen. It is erect, and may be larger, smaller or the same size as the object, so C and D are not general properties. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: cannot be formed on a screen
can be formed on a screen

questions.enonce_markdown:
When the speed of light reduces as it passes from one medium to another, the path of the light:

*Options as printed:* A) curves towards the normal.   B) curves away from the normal.   C) bends towards the normal.   D) bends away from the normal.
questions.corrige_markdown:
When light slows down on entering an optically denser medium (for example from air to glass or water) its path bends towards the normal, and the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence. Options A and C both say this in different words, and B and D say the opposite.

**Intended answer: A (curves towards the normal).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify which of the graphs in figure 2 shows how the temperature, $\theta$, of water during boiling varies with the time, $t$, of heating.

![fig-2](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: While water boils, the heat supplied is used to break the bonds between molecules (latent heat of vaporization) and not to raise the temperature, so $\theta$ stays constant at the boiling point. The graph is a horizontal line: graph D. Graph A would show the temperature rising steadily, B falling and C rising faster and faster. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of parallel connection of bulbs?
questions.corrige_markdown: In a parallel circuit each bulb is connected directly across the supply, so each has the full potential difference (D) and shines at its normal, brighter glow than bulbs in series (A); each branch has its own switch, so one bulb can be on while the others are off (B). The statement that one fuse protects all the bulbs is not an advantage of the parallel arrangement: a single fuse in the main line cannot protect the individual branches, which need a fuse of their own (it is a property of a series circuit, where the same current flows through all the bulbs). By elimination the answer is C. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: One bulb can be switched on while the others are off.
A fuse can be used to protect all the bulbs.
The bulbs are at the same potential difference.

questions.enonce_markdown: The heat energy needed to change the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by one unit is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Specific heat capacity is the quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ of a substance by $1\ \mathrm{K}$: $c = \dfrac{Q}{m\,\Delta\theta}$, in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. Heat capacity (C) refers to the whole body, not to a unit mass, and latent heats (A, B) are about changes of state with no change of temperature. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following factors affect the force between two charged bodies?
questions.corrige_markdown: The electrostatic force depends on the charges carried and on the distance between them: $F = \dfrac{k\,Q_1 Q_2}{d^2}$. Mass, weight and volume are not involved. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Isotopes of an element differ in terms of the number of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Isotopes are atoms of the same element, so they have the same number of protons (same atomic number) and the same number of electrons when neutral; they differ in the number of neutrons, hence in mass number (for example $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{14}\mathrm{C}$). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 3 shows three resistors connected in an electric circuit. The combined resistance of the resistors is:

![fig-3](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In the figure, $R_1$ and $R_3$ are in parallel and this pair is in series with $R_2$. The parallel pair has resistance $R_p$ with $\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_3}$, so $R_p = \dfrac{R_1 R_3}{R_1 + R_3}$. Adding the series resistor: $R = \dfrac{R_1 R_3}{R_1 + R_3} + R_2$. Option B uses the inverse of $R_p$, a common slip. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The right-hand-grip rule is used in the case of a coil to determine:
questions.corrige_markdown: For a coil (solenoid), the right-hand grip rule says: grip the coil with the fingers curled in the direction of the current; the thumb then points to the north pole of the electromagnet (the direction of the magnetic field inside the coil). It is therefore used to find the polarity of the magnet produced. The current direction is the data, not the result, and the rule says nothing about the duration of a force. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the motion of the magnetic field
the duration of the force produced
the polarity of the magnet produced.

questions.enonce_markdown: The heat energy required to change a unit mass of ice from when it just starts melting until it all turns to liquid is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The energy needed to change $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ of a solid at its melting point into liquid at the same temperature is the specific latent heat of fusion, $l_f = \dfrac{Q}{m}$, in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$ (for ice about $3.3 \times 10^5\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$). The latent heat of fusion (C) is the energy for the whole mass, not for a unit mass, and heat capacities (A, B) relate to a change of temperature. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the heat capacity of the water
the specific heat capacity of water
the latent heat of fusion of water
the specific latent heat of fusion of water

questions.enonce_markdown: When a cup of tea is stirred with a stainless steel spoon, the heat transfer processes involved are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Heat travels along the metal spoon by conduction; the hot tea circulates by convection, and the tea, the cup and the spoon give out infra-red waves, which is radiation. All three processes occur at once. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a polythene rod is rubbed with a dry woolen cloth, the cloth gives off electrons to the rod and becomes positively charged while the rod become negatively charged. The reason for this transfer of electrons is that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Electrons move from the material that holds them more loosely to the material that holds them more tightly. Here the electrons leave the wool and go to the polythene, so the electrons in the wool are more weakly held to their nuclei; the wool becomes positive and the polythene negative. The total number of electrons in each body is not the reason (A, B), and D states the opposite. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the woolen cloth has more electrons than the polythene rod
the polythene rod has more electrons than the woolen cloth
in the woolen cloth, the electron are more weakly held to the nucleus
in the polythene rod, the electrons are more weakly held to the nucleus

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the uses of hard magnetic materials is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Hard magnetic materials (steel, alnico) are hard to magnetize but keep their magnetism, so they are used to make permanent magnets. Soft magnetic materials (soft iron) are used for the cores of electromagnets and transformers because they magnetize and demagnetize easily. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A virtual image is an image that:
questions.corrige_markdown: A virtual image is formed by rays that only appear to diverge from a point, so no light actually reaches it and it cannot be shown on a screen. It is formed on the same side of the lens as the object (so C is false) and it is not always bigger than the object. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: cannot be formed on a screen
can be formed on a screen
is formed on the opposite side of the lens

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which graph in figure 4 best represents the velocity-time graph for a stone that is dropped from a height?

![fig-4](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: A stone dropped from rest falls with the constant acceleration due to gravity $g$, so $v = gt$: velocity increases uniformly from zero and the velocity-time graph is a straight line through the origin, graph D. Graph A shows a body slowing down, graph B a body that reaches a terminal velocity (large air resistance) and graph C an acceleration that keeps increasing. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A trolley of mass 500 g is accelerated at $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. The force that produced the acceleration is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Convert the mass to kilograms: $500\ \mathrm{g} = 0.5\ \mathrm{kg}$. By Newton's second law $F = ma = 0.5 \times 10 = 5\ \mathrm{N}$. Option D comes from using $500$ instead of $0.5$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
When two person sleep under the blanket, they feel hot because:

*Options as printed:* A) the blanket supplies heat to them   B) the blanket absorbs cold from them   C) the blanket prevent heat from leaving their bodies   D) the blanket traps the heat they produce
questions.corrige_markdown:
The bodies of the sleepers produce heat. A blanket is a poor conductor (it traps layers of air, which are good insulators), so it reduces the heat lost from their bodies to the surroundings and they stay warm. A blanket does not supply heat (A) and cold is not a substance that can be absorbed (B). Options C and D describe the same effect in different words.

**Intended answer: C (the blanket prevent heat from leaving their bodies).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The principle of conservation of linear momentum states that:
questions.corrige_markdown: The principle states that the total linear momentum of a system is constant provided no external force acts on it, that is for a closed (isolated) system: in a collision, the total momentum before equals the total momentum after. Option D gives this statement with its condition. Options B and C speak only of the initial or only of the final momentum, and option A omits the condition that no external force acts. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the sum of initial momentum is equal to the sum of final momentum
the total initial momentum of a system is constant
the total final momentum of a system is constant
the total momentum of a closed system is constant

questions.enonce_markdown: When a car is moving with constant velocity:
questions.corrige_markdown: Constant velocity means zero acceleration, and by Newton's second law $F = ma$ the net force is zero (the driving force balances friction and air resistance). A constant but non-zero net force (A) would give a constant acceleration and a changing velocity. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A radioactive atom $^{124}_{56}\mathrm{Y}$ decays to $^{120}_{54}\mathrm{X}$ by emitting a particle z as shown in the equation below:

$$
^{124}_{56}\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow {}^{120}_{54}\mathrm{X} + z.
$$

The particle z is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Conserve the mass number and the proton number. Mass number: $124 = 120 + A_z$, so $A_z = 4$. Proton number: $56 = 54 + Z_z$, so $Z_z = 2$. A particle with mass number 4 and charge $+2$ is a helium nucleus, $^4_2\mathrm{He}$: an alpha particle. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When an intrinsic semiconductor is heated, its conductivity:
questions.corrige_markdown: In an intrinsic (pure) semiconductor heat gives more valence electrons enough energy to break free, which creates more free electrons and holes. More charge carriers means a larger conductivity, so the conductivity increases with temperature (unlike a metal, whose resistance rises when heated). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a converging lens of focal length 20 cm. The image formed will be:
questions.corrige_markdown: Here $u = f = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$. Using $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{v}$ gives $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{20} = 0$, so $v$ is infinite. An object at the principal focus sends out a parallel beam after the lens, so the image is formed at infinity. Option D (40 cm behind the lens) is the image position for an object placed at $2f = 40\ \mathrm{cm}$, not at 20 cm. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: 20 cm in front of the lens

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 43 - 46

Figure 5 is a diagram that was used to investigate the variation of fundamental frequency with the length of a vibrating string.

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

Which of the following quantities is kept constant during the exercise?

*Options as printed:* A) Mass   B) Tension   C) Amplitude   D) Wave length
questions.corrige_markdown:
To find how the fundamental frequency depends on the length, only the length is changed (by moving the movable bridge); the other factors that fix the frequency of the string must be kept constant: the tension in the string (given by the same slotted masses hanging from it) and the mass per unit length of the string. The wavelength of the fundamental is $\lambda = 2l$, so it changes with the length, and the amplitude is not controlled.

**Intended answer: B (Tension).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 43 - 46 (Figure 5)

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

The paper rider is thrown off when:
questions.corrige_markdown: The tuning fork forces the string to vibrate. When the length is adjusted so that the natural frequency of the string equals the frequency of the fork, resonance occurs: the string vibrates with a large amplitude and an antinode forms under the paper rider, which is thrown off. If the frequencies differ (C) the string vibrates weakly and the rider stays on; a node (D) is a point that does not move, so a rider placed on it would stay. **Answer: A.**

Questions 43 - 46 (Figure 5)

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

The relationship between frequency and length of a vibrating string is given as:
questions.corrige_markdown: For a stretched string the fundamental frequency is $f = \dfrac{1}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$. With the tension $T$ and the mass per unit length $\mu$ constant, $f \propto \dfrac{1}{l}$: a shorter string gives a higher note, so $f \times l$ is constant. **Answer: D.**

Questions 47 - 50

Figure 6 shows an electrical transmission system. M, N and P are electrical devices while R is a radio set.

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

The function of M and N in the set up in figure 6 is:
questions.corrige_markdown: M is the transformer of the production unit: its secondary coil has more turns than its primary, so it steps the voltage up for transmission (high voltage, low current, small $I^2R$ loss in the cables). N is the transformer of the consumption unit: its primary has more turns than its secondary, so it steps the voltage down to a safe value for the radio set. Voltages are stepped up or down, and the current changes in the opposite way, so B and D, which speak only of current, do not describe the function. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: M steps up voltages while N steps down voltages
M steps up current while N steps down current
M steps down voltages while N steps up voltages
M steps down current while N steps up current

Questions 47 - 50 (Figure 6)

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

M does not function on direct current, (d.c.) because:
questions.corrige_markdown: A transformer works by electromagnetic induction: an e.m.f. is induced in the secondary coil only when the magnetic flux linked with it changes. Direct current is steady, so it produces a constant flux whose change is zero (negligible) and no e.m.f. is induced in the secondary; an alternating current produces a continuously changing flux. The size of the d.c. voltage is not the cause (A), and a d.c. does not cause a large change of flux (D). **Answer: C.**

M steps up current while N steps down current
the change in magnetic flux produced by the d.c is negligible.
the change in magnetic flux produced by the d.c is high, thus can burn M

The device labelled P is a:
questions.corrige_markdown: P is drawn with the diode symbol (a triangle pointing to a bar) in series with the radio set R. A diode lets current pass in one direction only, so here it rectifies the a.c. from the transformer N into d.c. for the radio. A resistor would be drawn as a rectangle (R in the figure). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 47 - 50 (Figure 6)

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

The resistance of the transmission cable is low in order to:
questions.corrige_markdown: The power wasted as heat in the cables is $P = I^2R$. Making the resistance $R$ of the transmission cables low reduces this loss, which is the main purpose of low-resistance cables (together with the high-voltage transmission that lowers $I$). Diverting excess current to the earth (A) is the job of the earth wire and fuse; a 'current drop' (B) is not a quantity used in this context. A low resistance also lowers the voltage drop $IR$ along the cable (D), but the reason usually given is the reduction of power loss. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: divert excess or high currents to the earth
